title.narrative: Output 7.5. Increased capacity of Member States to develop fair and effective labour migration frameworks, institutions and services to protect migrant workers

description.narrative: Migrant workers and their families have better access to services through the institutionalization and operationalization of Migrant Resource Centers in Quezon City, Negros Occidental Province, and Tabaco City, Albay – the MRC in Quezon City was established in 2022, and is the first in the Metro Manila region. Case management and services to migrant workers are complemented by community outreach, reintegration support services for returning migrant workers; in 2022, financial literacy skills are being provided to migrant workers–. Through their work, the MRCs have been able to provide 2,936 migrant workers (2,191 women) information and services. The partnership has contributed to LGUs prioritizing migration agenda as evident in formulating migration- related policies and implementation of programmes and services to migrant workers and families through regular programming. With the support of the EU, ILO undertook a partnership with LGUs to set up the MRCs in the LGUs and advocated for inclusion of these services in the budgets of these LGUs. ILO further supported the capacity-building of MRC service providers in facilitating gender-responsive case management to OFWs, especially women; improving migration-related data documentation and reporting through updating of case documentation forms and reporting templates and developing online database/registries; increasing public awareness on labour migration; and formulating migration-related policies for better protection of migrant workers and their families. Technical assistance was also provided during the Strategic Planning Workshop of the TWG of Quezon City Migration and Development Council in June 2022 to mainstream the migration agenda. In consultation with stakeholders, ILO supported the development of the Manual of Operations of MRCs operating in the Philippines with reference to international labour standards and guidelines. The MRC Manual of Operations was completed in December 2023.

description.narrative: Republic Act 11641 creating the new Department of Migrant Workers came into effect on 3 Feb 2022. The Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) were adopted by the Philippine Government on 4 April 2022 informed by consultations with social partners and guided by international labour standards. According to the IRR, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) serves as the primary, and central government agency to protect the rights and promote the welfare of overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) regardless of status. The DMW is mandated to formulate, coordinate, administer and implement labour migration policies and programmes, including regulating and managing the recruitment and overseas employment of OFWs, prescribing and providing services for OFWs and their families at all stages of migration including in cases of violence and exploitation, and facilitating/promoting full-cycle reintegration, social protection and skills development of returning migrant workers. DMW absorbed and consolidated the labour migration functions, mandates and resources previously assigned to several government offices/units. This overhauls the Philippine labour migration system and governance based on the 1995 Magna Carta of Migrant Workers (RA 8042, as amended). The DMW will improve the coordination and the interventions being provided to migrant workers. The DMW has also committed to taking a gender-responsive approach to better serve women migrant workers’ needs. In 2022, the Implementing Rules and Regulations for Ordinance No. SP 2500, S-2016 Creating the Quezon City Migrant Resource Center (MRC) were adopted and the Quezon City Draft Memorandum of Agreement (MOA)/MOU with the United Domestic Workers of the Philippines (UNITED) was agreed, strengthening rights-based, gender-responsive Migrant Resource Centers in Quezon City (National Capital Region). ILO facilitated five tripartite-plus consultations on the IRR with 470 tripartite-plus stakeholders; gathered stakeholders' recommendations and helped put these together as submissions/interventions in the Congressional hearings; gave technical inputs to strengthen alignment with international labour standards, enhance gender responsiveness; submitted technical comments and made interventions (including by the ILO migration specialist) at the Congressional hearings. ILO also facilitated consultative processes in gathering inputs and recommendations of social partners for the crafting of the IRR, focusing on key provisions; gender dimensions; and recruitment, reintegration and welfare aspects of the law guided by international labour standards. ILO helped review the draft local ordinances/issuances, gave technical inputs and recommendations on aligning these with national laws and international standards, enhance rights-based and gender-responsive framework, and ensure participation/representation of social partners, particularly OFWs.
